# Next.js Engineering Rules

## App Router & Project Structure

- Use the App Router (`app/`) exclusively. Do not mix App Router and Pages Router (`pages/`) in the same project.
- Organize routes by feature domain under `app/`. Avoid deeply nested catch-all segments; prefer explicit route groups with `(group)` folders.
- Colocate route-specific components, hooks, and utilities inside the route segment directory. Only promote to `shared/` when two or more routes consume the same module.
- Name the root layout `app/layout.tsx`. Every nested layout must be an explicit `layout.tsx` file; do not define layout-level UI inside `page.tsx`.
- Use `loading.tsx` for streaming suspense boundaries and `error.tsx` for error boundaries at every route segment that performs async data access.
- Use `not-found.tsx` to render explicit 404 UI instead of relying on the global 404 fallback.

## Server Components vs. Client Components

- Default to React Server Components (RSC). Opt into Client Components (`"use client"`) only when the module requires browser APIs, event handlers, or client-side state.
- Never mark a component as a Client Component solely because a child needs interactivity. Push `"use client"` to the leaf that actually needs it and keep parent components as Server Components.
- Do not import server-only modules (database clients, secret readers, file system access) inside Client Components. Use `server-only` package imports to enforce this boundary at build time.
- Pass serializable props from Server Components to Client Components. Functions, class instances, and non-serializable objects must not cross the server–client boundary.
- Access cookies, headers, and server-side context via `next/headers` inside Server Components or Route Handlers only. Never access them inside Client Components.

## Data Fetching

- Fetch data at the Server Component level closest to where it is rendered. Avoid prop-drilling fetched data through multiple layers.
- Use `async/await` directly in Server Components for data fetching. Do not use `useEffect` for initial data loading in Server Components.
- Deduplicate requests using React's built-in `fetch` cache. Do not re-fetch the same resource in multiple components within the same render.
- Tag `fetch` calls with `cache: 'force-cache'`, `cache: 'no-store'`, or `next: { revalidate: N }` based on the data's freshness requirements. The default caching behavior must be explicit, never assumed.
- Use Server Actions for mutations. Do not create API routes solely to handle form submissions or button-triggered mutations from the same application.
- Validate all Server Action inputs with a schema (e.g., Zod) before processing. Server Actions are a public boundary; treat input as untrusted.

## Route Handlers & API Layer

- Place Route Handlers in `app/api/` only for endpoints consumed by external clients, third-party webhooks, or mobile apps. Internal data needs are served directly from Server Components or Server Actions.
- Export only the HTTP methods the route supports. Do not export a catch-all handler and switch on `request.method` inside.
- Return typed `NextResponse` objects with explicit status codes. Do not return raw objects or rely on implicit 200 responses.
- Authenticate and authorize every Route Handler at the entry point before processing the request body. Do not defer auth checks to the service layer.

## Rendering Strategy & Caching

- Use Static Site Generation (SSG) for content that does not change per request. Use `generateStaticParams` to pre-render all known dynamic segments at build time.
- Use Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) for content that changes infrequently. Set `revalidate` based on acceptable staleness, not on convenience.
- Use dynamic rendering (`cache: 'no-store'` or `cookies()`/`headers()` access) only for content that is genuinely personalized or request-specific.
- Do not opt an entire layout or page into dynamic rendering to avoid configuring caching. Isolate the dynamic component and wrap it in `<Suspense>`.
- Use `unstable_cache` from `next/cache` to cache the result of expensive server-side computations across requests. Tag caches for targeted invalidation via `revalidateTag`.

## Metadata & SEO

- Export a `metadata` object or `generateMetadata` function from every `page.tsx` and `layout.tsx`. Never leave title or description undefined.
- Use `generateMetadata` for dynamic routes where metadata depends on fetched data. Avoid hardcoded metadata on dynamic pages.
- Set canonical URLs via `alternates.canonical` in metadata. Do not rely on the CDN or reverse proxy to set canonical headers.
- Use `next/og` for Open Graph image generation. Do not serve static OG images for dynamic content.

## Image & Font Optimization

- Use `next/image` for all raster images. Do not use raw `<img>` tags except for inline SVGs or externally hosted images where `next/image` is not applicable.
- Define `sizes` on every `next/image` to match the CSS layout width. Omitting `sizes` causes the browser to request the largest image variant.
- Specify `priority` only on above-the-fold images critical to LCP. Do not apply `priority` broadly.
- Load all fonts via `next/font`. Do not use `<link rel="stylesheet">` for web fonts; doing so prevents font display optimization and introduces layout shift.

## Middleware

- Use `middleware.ts` only for cross-cutting concerns: authentication redirects, A/B routing, geolocation, and request header injection.
- Keep Middleware logic minimal and free of database calls or heavy computation. Middleware runs on every matched request in the Edge Runtime.
- Use `matcher` config in Middleware to restrict execution to relevant route patterns. Do not run Middleware on static asset paths or API routes that handle their own auth.
- Do not use Middleware as a substitute for server-side authorization inside Route Handlers or Server Actions. Middleware is a routing layer, not a security layer.

## Performance & Bundle Management

- Analyze the client bundle with `@next/bundle-analyzer` before every major release. No new third-party library may be added to the client bundle without an explicit size review.
- Dynamically import heavy Client Components with `next/dynamic` and `{ ssr: false }` when they are not needed on initial render.
- Avoid importing large libraries (e.g., `lodash`, `moment`) wholesale. Import only the specific function needed, or replace with a lighter alternative.
- Eliminate unused exports. Tree-shaking only removes dead code when exports are explicit; barrel files with wildcard re-exports defeat it.

## Error Handling & Observability

- Instrument Server Components and Server Actions with structured error logging that includes route, user context (non-PII), and a correlation ID.
- Use `error.tsx` boundaries to display actionable recovery UI. Never expose raw error messages or stack traces to the client.
- Track Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, INP) using `next/web-vitals` or an observability integration. Regressions in CWV metrics must block release.

## Security

- Set `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, and `Referrer-Policy` headers in `next.config.ts` under `headers()`. Do not rely solely on hosting platform defaults.
- Never expose secret environment variables to the client. Only variables prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` are safe for client-side access; treat all others as server-only.
- Validate and sanitize all user-supplied input in Server Actions and Route Handlers before use. Apply allow-list validation, not deny-list.
- Use `CSRF` protection for Server Actions when the application supports cookie-based sessions accessible from JavaScript.
